editorial:
Imagine the stress of bringing your partner home to meet your parents, but add a giant language gap and two very different cultures. You get a hilarious and sweet ride as a woman tries to play translator between her traditional Chinese father and her Jewish-American boyfriend. She basically makes up her own version of what they are saying to keep the peace, telling her dad that her boyfriend is more traditional than he is, while telling her boyfriend that her dad actually loves him. It feels like a chaotic family dinner that you can't stop watching, mixing awkward silences with big laughs.

The acting is top-notch because the actors make the confusing conversations feel real and funny. The pacing is quick, so you never feel bored, though some of the lies get a bit too wild to believe. If you have ever felt like the middleman in your own family, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the funny facial expressions, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night with your partner.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the dad reveals he has been using a translation app on his phone the whole time. He knew exactly what the boyfriend was saying, and he actually liked him more than the daughter realized. The three of them finally stop pretending and have an honest talk about their differences. It ends with a big family meal where they laugh about the lies, showing that love is more important than a perfect translation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and stories about cultural clashes.
